claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child I'm responsible for. I have one child, Alex, who is 20 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to understand a bit more about Alex's situation.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I have a few more questions to fully assess the situation.

Is Alex currently registered with the Career Service or Careers Wales, and are they waiting to start approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't registered with the careers service or anything like that. They just finished their education a while back.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just to be thorough, I need to ask:

Does Alex have any disabilities or health conditions, and if so, are they in receipt of certain disability benefits such as Disability Living Allowance or Personal Independence Payment?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't have any disabilities or health conditions, and they're not receiving any benefits like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me also confirm a couple more details:

Are you currently responsible for Alex - meaning Alex lives with you and you're contributing to their upbringing or care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. Alex lives at home with me, and I'm responsible for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question to complete my assessment:

Do you normally live in the UK, or are you subject to immigration control that would prevent you from claiming benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm not subject to any immigration control.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: Child Benefit is generally only payable for children under 16 years old, or for young people aged 16-19 (in some cases up to their 20th birthday) if they are in approved education or training. Since Alex is 20 years old and is not currently in approved education or training, not registered with a careers service waiting to start such education or training, and doesn't have a disability that would extend eligibility, Alex has exceeded the age limit for Child Benefit.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future - for example, if they were to start approved education or training before turning 20 - the situation might be different. However, based on the current circumstances you've described, Child Benefit is not available.

Is there anything else I can help clarify?
